subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw expose cross-session run progress through a new `sessions_subscribe`/`agent.events` contract, and what observer authorization, redaction, retention, replay, and channel delivery rules must gate it?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the implementation creates a new cross-session visibility boundary and model-facing API, so automation should not choose the permanent contract or security policy.

options.title: Add Permission-Checked Subscription Contract
options.body: Create a bounded run-event observation API and tool that derives observer rights from session visibility/A2A policy and sanitizes event payloads before replay or delivery.

options.title: Land Only Timeout/Ack Slices
options.body: Keep progress streaming out of scope while reviewing separate timeout-compensation or handoff-acknowledgement PRs on their own narrower contracts.

options.title: Defer Core Progress API
options.body: Document the current fire-and-forget, wait, history, and final-announce behavior while leaving real-time inter-session progress unsupported for now.

recommendation.title: Add Permission-Checked Subscription Contract
recommendation.body: Create a bounded run-event observation API and tool that derives observer rights from session visibility/A2A policy and sanitizes event payloads before replay or delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: The sessions_send, agent.wait, inter-session provenance, and agent-event history most directly route this API/security decision to steipete.
